headline: Medium prompt-injection and capability-conflict risk from shared file-based workflows; no direct evidence of a dangerous default bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a writes and reads files and its sandboxing says skills “reference each other and build on shared context,” while agent_b is a memory layer with no documented isolation or provenance controls. That creates a plausible default path where attacker-controlled content from agent_a can be treated as trusted input by agent_b. The pairwise interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs content into a shared workspace that agent_b later ingests as instructions
IF agent_b consumes untrusted file content without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Add a manual review step before agent_b consumes agent_a outputs
Prefix agent_a outputs with non-executable delimiters
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all cross-agent artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a can read and write the filesystem and touches marketing content, but agent_b has network_egress none and no documented file surfaces or sensitive data classes. The main leakage path is a shared workspace exposing agent_a content to agent_b, but the blast radius appears limited to marketing/product-marketing material rather than regulated data. No direct evidence shows either agent uploads data by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF agent_b is configured to read agent_a-generated files
mitigations: Use separate workspaces
Restrict agent_a output to non-sensitive drafts
Review shared files before handoff
Turn off any automatic file sync
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and supports multiple instances; agent_b has no declared locking or concurrency controls. If both are attached to the same mutable workspace, concurrent edits can collide even though agent_b’s write surface is undocumented. Because the overlap is plausible but not fully specified, uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same writable directory
IF agent_a runs multiple instances against the same files
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize runs with a simple lock file
Avoid concurrent edits to shared artifacts
Check in changes one agent at a time
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces marketing content and product marketing context, which agent_b could plausibly store or reuse as memory. If agent_b treats that output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into later work products. There is no documented verification step between them, so the pathway exists by inference and merits medium severity.
conditions: IF agent_b stores agent_a output as durable memory
IF downstream tasks rely on that memory without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before memory writes
Tag agent_a outputs as unverified
Keep source citations alongside stored notes
Limit agent_b to summarization only
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds for memory ingestion

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class, residency mismatch, or retention-policy conflict is documented in either profile. agent_a touches marketing content only, and agent_b lists no data classes touched. With no evidence of PHI, EU PII, or special compliance obligations, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either profile is updated to include regulated data classes
IF a residency or retention policy is later documented as conflicting
mitigations: Document data classes for both agents
Confirm retention settings before deployment
Review residency requirements if scope changes
Keep regulated data out of this pair
requires-engineering: add compliance policy checks
